title: Cap. VIII Arg.: if God elects and reprobates without cause from men, he is acceptor of persons (Acts 10:34)
pass_a_gloss: If God from eternity were to elect certain ones, to reprobate certain ones, without a cause holding itself on the part of men, then he would be an acceptor of persons. For he seems to be an acceptor of persons, who, two existing equal, gives to one what he denies to the other. But this respect of persons is removed from God, Acts 10:34.
pass_b_english: Argument: if from eternity God elected some and reprobated others without a cause holding on the human side, then he would be an acceptor of persons. For he seems an acceptor of persons who, when two are equal, gives to one what he denies the other. But that respect of persons is removed from God (Acts 10:34).
source_text: Si Deus aliquos eligeret ab aeterno, aliquos reprobaret, absque causa se tenente ex parte hominum, tunc esset acceptor personarum. Videtur enim esse acceptor personarum, qui, duobus existentibus aequalibus, uni dat quod alteri denegat. Haec autem προσωπολημψία a Deo removetur, Actor. x. 34.
